problem:
Construct the matrix $T$ of the linear transformation $T$ that acts on a vector in ${R}^{2}$ as follows (in the order given):

- It stretches the result by a scale factor of $4$ parallel to the $y$-axis, then

- shears the result with a shear factor of $1$ parallel to the $x$-axis, and finally

- scales the result by a scale factor of $3$ with the center of enlargement at the origin.

|  |  | {{field-1}} | {{field-2}} |  |
| --- | --- | --- | --- | --- |
| $T=\,\,$ |  |  |  |  |
|  |  | {{field-3}} | {{field-4}} |  |

feedback.problem:
Construct the matrix $T$ of the linear transformation $T$ that acts on a vector in ${R}^{2}$ as follows (in the order given):

- It stretches the result by a scale factor of $3$ parallel to the $x$-axis, then

- shears the result with a shear factor of $2$ parallel to the $y$-axis, and finally

- reflects the result about the $x$-axis.

|  |  | {{field-1}} | {{field-2}} |  |
| --- | --- | --- | --- | --- |
| $T=\,\,$ |  |  |  |  |
|  |  | {{field-3}} | {{field-4}} |  |
feedback.worked_solution:
Let $P$ be the matrix that represents the stretching, $Q$ be the matrix that represents the shearing, and $R$ be the matrix that represents the reflection. These are given by the following elementary transformation matrices:

$$
P=[\begin{aligned}3 & 0 \\ 0 & 1\end{aligned}],\,Q=[\begin{aligned}1 & 0 \\ 2 & 1\end{aligned}],\,R=[\begin{aligned}1 & 0 \\ 0 & -1\end{aligned}]\,\,
$$

Hence, the combined transformation can be represented by the matrix $RQP:$

$$
\begin{aligned}T & =RQP \\  & =[\begin{aligned}1 & 0 \\ 0 & -1\end{aligned}][\begin{aligned}1 & 0 \\ 2 & 1\end{aligned}][\begin{aligned}3 & 0 \\ 0 & 1\end{aligned}] \\  & =[\begin{aligned}1 & 0 \\ -2 & -1\end{aligned}][\begin{aligned}3 & 0 \\ 0 & 1\end{aligned}] \\  & =[\begin{aligned}3 & 0 \\ -6 & -1\end{aligned}]\end{aligned}
$$
